title: Leakage-controlled tuning and control-arm protocol for temporal re-ranking claims
description: Make the evaluation protocol itself a contribution: tune the temporal weight lambda only on a held-out question split; add controls that randomly permute version timestamps across candidate passages and that shift query dates by a fixed offset so elapsed-time order no longer aligns with in-force order; add a content-blind date-only ranker that scores passages using timestamps alone. Report the full lambda sensitivity curve rather than the argmax, and report version-selection accuracy and answer accuracy separately.
why_differs: TempRALM selects its temporal scaling factor for relative importance with no reported held-out validation or content-blind control, and Prior et al. have no soft re-ranking arm to control at all. This modification makes explicit the controls that both lines of work leave implicit.
technical_mechanism: Data-level controls (permuted timestamps, shifted query dates) plus a date-only scoring arm; protocol-level control by tuning lambda on a held-out split and reporting the sensitivity curve instead of a single tuned value.
expected_benefit: Establishes whether any observed temporal gain is genuine retrieval skill or a timestamp shortcut; without it the hypothesis is not testable. A protocol of this kind is also reusable for any future versioned-document retrieval work.
potential_novelty: Hedged: neither retrieved paper reports leakage controls for a temporal weight, but benchmark-methodology novelty is inherently weaker and reviewers may treat it as standard good practice rather than a contribution.
implementation_difficulty_basis: All components are simple data transformations and score re-computation on top of the existing pipeline; no modelling, index rebuild or extra data acquisition is needed.
experimental_difficulty_basis: The controls are cheap to implement and run, but they require a held-out split, a shuffled-timestamp corpus clone and careful per-regime reporting, which adds orchestration rather than new resources.
main_risk: The protocol may show that the soft temporal term has no effect at all, which would be a scientifically useful but not a positive contribution on its own.
required_baselines: Shuffled-timestamp variant of every temporal arm
